<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:ODE}
  Let $r\in[1,\infty]$, $\boldsymbol{u}= (u_t,u_x) \in [1,\infty]^2$, $\boldsymbol{v} = (v_t,v_x) \in [1,\infty]^2$, $\kappa, M \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ and $m\in (0,\infty)$.
  We say that a {subadditive} operator $T\colon L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+) \to L^0(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ is  a
  \emph{{singular operator of type} $(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v, M)$} if there exists a constant {$C<\infty$} 
   such that the following assertions hold for all $f \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ and all rectangles ${\boldsymbol{E}},{\boldsymbol{F}}\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$ in the following configurations. 
  \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item\label{it:ODEDef1} {(Local boundedness on Whitney-type regions)}
      {If ${\boldsymbol{F}}={\boldsymbol{E}}$, $c\cdot  \ell_x \leq \ell_t^{\frac1m} \leq \ell_x$ and       
      $\inf(E_t) \geq c^m \cdot \ell_t$,} then
\begin{align*}
    \bigl\| \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}})\bigr\|_{L^r_{t,x}} \leq C\cdot \inf(E_t)^{\kappa} \cdot \bigl\| f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}}\bigr\|_{L^r_{t,x}}.
\end{align*} 
      \item\label{it:ODEDef2}  ($t$-separation) 
      {If $c\cdot  \ell_x \leq \ell_t^{\frac1m} \leq \ell_x$ and $d(E_t,F_t)\ge c^m \cdot \ell_t$,} then
      \begin{align*}
  \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})\bigr\|_{L^{v_t}_tL^{v_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}} 
  &
  \leq C\cdot {d(E_t,F_t)^{-[u_t,v_t]-\frac nm[u_x,v_x]+\kappa}}
\cdot \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}}\bigr\|_{L^{u_t}_tL^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}.
\end{align*}
  \item\label{it:ODEDef3}  ($t$- and $x$-separation)
    {If $\ell_t^{\frac1m} \leq \ell_x$, $d(E_t,F_t)\ge c^m\cdot \ell_t$ and $d(E_x,F_x)\ge c\cdot  \ell_x$,}
    then
\begin{align*}
  \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})\bigr\|_{L^{v_t}_tL^{v_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}} \leq C&\cdot   {d(E_x,F_x)^{-m[u_t,v_t]-{n}[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa}}
  \cdot  \Bigl(\frac{\operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)}{d(E_x,F_x)^{m}}\Bigr)^M 
\cdot \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}}\bigr\|_{L^{u_t}_tL^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}.
\end{align*}
    \item\label{it:ODEDef4}  ($x$-separation)
    {If $\ell_t^{\frac1m}\leq \ell_x$ and $d(E_x,F_x)\ge c \cdot \ell_x$,} then
\begin{align*}
  \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})\bigr\|_{L^{r_{\vphantom{t}}}_{\vphantom{t}t}L^{v_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}} \leq C
  \cdot   {d(E_x,F_x)^{-{n}[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa}}
  \cdot  \Bigl(\frac{\operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)}{d(E_x,F_x)^{m}}\Bigr)^{M+[u_t,v_t]} 
\cdot \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}}\bigr\|_{L^{r_{\vphantom{t}}}_{\vphantom{t}t}L^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}.
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:SIO-simple}
 Let $r\in[1,\infty]$, $\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v} \in [1,\infty]^2$ with $u_t \le r \le v_t$, $\kappa, M \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ and $m\in (0,\infty)$. Let $T$ be a bounded subadditive operator from $L^r(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+; t^{\gamma r}\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x)$ to $L^r(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+^{1+n}; t^{(\gamma-\kappa) r}\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x)$ for some $\gamma\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$.  If for any $f \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$, and any  rectangles $\boldE,\boldF \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$ satisfying one of the conditions
 \begin{itemize}
     \item  ($t$-separation) 
      {$c\cdot  \ell_x \leq \ell_t^{\frac1m} \leq \ell_x$ and $d(E_t,F_t)\ge c^m \cdot \ell_t$,}
      \item  ($x$-separation)
    $\ell_t^{\frac1m}\leq \ell_x$ and $d(E_x,F_x)\ge c \cdot \ell_x,$
 \end{itemize} we have the inequality
\begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \label{eq:odeprototype}
\bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}}T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})\bigr\|_{L^{v_t}_tL^{v_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}
\leq C\cdot \bigl(d(E_t,F_t)^{\frac1m}&+d(E_x,F_x)\bigr)^{-m[u_t,v_t]-n[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa}\\
&\quad \cdot \Bigl(1+\frac{d(E_x,F_x)^m}{\operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)}\Bigr)^{-M}
\cdot \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}}\bigr\|_{L^{u_t}_tL^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}},\end{aligned}
\end{equation}    
    then $T$ is a singular operator of type $(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v},M)$.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The assumed boundedness of $T$ implies Definition \ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef1} since $\sup(E_t)\eqsim t \eqsim \inf(E_t)$ for all $t \in E_t$. Next, 
   in the configuration in \ref{it:ODEDef2} we have\begin{align*}
       d(E_x,F_x) &\le \ell_{x}\eqsim \ell_{t}^{1/m}\eqsim d(E_t,F_t)^{1/m}\\
       \operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)&\ge  d(E_t,F_t) \eqsim \ell_{t}\gtrsim d(E_x,F_x)^m
   \end{align*} and thus \eqref{eq:odeprototype} implies Definition \ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef2}. Definition \ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef3} follows similarly. Finally in the configuration in \ref{it:ODEDef4}, together with $u_t\leq r\leq v_t$ and H\"older's inequality, we have 
    \begin{align*}
        \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})\bigr\|_{L^{r_{\vphantom{x}}}_tL^{v_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}} &\leq |F_t|^{[r,v_t]} \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})\bigr\|_{L^{v_t}_t L^{v_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}} ,\\
        \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}}\bigr\|_{L^{u_t}_tL^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}} &\leq |E_t|^{[u_t,r]} \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}}\bigr\|_{L^{r_{\vphantom{x}}}_tL^{u_{x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}.
    \end{align*}
    Since $|F_t|,|E_{t}|\le \operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)$, $[u_t,r],[r,v_t] \ge 0$ and $[u_t,r]+[r,v_t]=[u_t,v_t]$, combining these two estimates with \eqref{eq:odeprototype}   yields  Definition \ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef4}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:ODE-contraction}  Let $r\in[1,\infty]$, $\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v} \in [1,\infty]^2$, $\kappa, M \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ and $m\in (0,\infty)$.
    Let $T$ be a singular operator of type $(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v,M)$. If $\widetilde{\boldsymbol u},\widetilde{\boldsymbol v} \in [1,\infty]^2$ satisfy
    \[
        u_t\leq \widetilde u_t\leq \widetilde v_t\leq v_t,
        \qquad
        u_x\leq \widetilde u_x\leq \widetilde v_x\leq v_x,
    \]
    then $T$ is a singular operator of type
    $(\kappa,m,r,\widetilde{\boldsymbol u},\widetilde{\boldsymbol v},M+[u_t,v_t]-[\widetilde u_t,\widetilde v_t])$.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Let ${\boldsymbol E}, {\boldsymbol F}\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+^{1+n}$ be rectangles. By
    H\"older's inequality, we have for $f \in L^\infty_c\br{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}$
    \begin{align*}
      \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol F} f\bigr\|_{L^{\widetilde v_t}_tL^{\widetilde v_x}_x}
      &\leq
      |F_t|^{[\widetilde v_t,v_t]}|F_x|^{[\widetilde v_x,v_x]}
      \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol F} f\bigr\|_{L^{v_t}_tL^{v_x}_x},\\
      \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E}\bigr\|_{L^{u_t}_tL^{u_x}_x}
      &\leq
      |E_t|^{[u_t,\widetilde u_t]}|E_x|^{[u_x,\widetilde u_x]}
      \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E}\bigr\|_{L^{\widetilde u_t}_tL^{\widetilde u_x}_x}.
    \end{align*}
We check each of the  configurations in Definition~\ref{def:ODE} separately.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item The local Whitney estimate is
    unchanged, since it only involves the exponent $r$.
    \item We have
    $|E_t|,|F_t|\lesssim d(E_t,F_t)$ and
    $|E_x|,|F_x|\lesssim d(E_t,F_t)^{n/m}$. Combining these bounds with the
    estimate for the original exponents changes the decay powers exactly from
    $[u_t,v_t]$ and $[u_x,v_x]$ to
    $[\widetilde u_t,\widetilde v_t]$ and
    $[\widetilde u_x,\widetilde v_x]$.
    \item We similarly use
    $|E_x|,|F_x|\lesssim d(E_x,F_x)^n$ and
    $|E_t|,|F_t|\leq \operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)$. Since 
    \[
       \operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)^{[u_t,v_t]-[\widetilde u_t,\widetilde v_t]}  =  d(E_x,F_x)^{m( [u_t,v_t]-[\widetilde u_t,\widetilde v_t])}\Bigl(\frac{\operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)}{d(E_x,F_x)^m}\Bigr)^{[u_t,v_t]-[\widetilde u_t,\widetilde v_t]},
    \]
    we obtain the claimed increase in $M$.
    \item H\"older's inequality is only needed in the
    spatial variable, because the time exponent is fixed at $r$ on both sides of
    Definition~\ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef4}. The spatial powers contract as above.
    Since
    \[
        M+[u_t,v_t]=\bigl(M+[u_t,v_t]-[\widetilde u_t,\widetilde v_t]\bigr)+[\widetilde u_t,\widetilde v_t],
    \]
    we also obtain exactly the right decay parameter.
\end{enumerate}
 This proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:boundedimplySOwithM=0}
Let $\boldsymbol p,\boldsymbol q\in [1,\infty]^2$ with $p_t\leq q_t$ and $p_x\leq q_x$, and let $m \in (0,\infty)$. Let
$T$ be a bounded subadditive operator from
$L^{p_t}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+;L^{p_x}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n))$ to $L^{q_t}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+;L^{q_x}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n))$. Set
\[
    \kappa:= [p_t,q_t]+\tfrac nm[p_x,q_x].
\]
Then $T$ is a singular operator of type
$(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v,[p_t,q_t]-[u_t,v_t])$ for all $r\in[1,\infty]$ and
$\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v\in[1,\infty]^2$ satisfying
\(
    p_t\leq u_t\leq r\leq v_t\leq q_t\), and \(
    p_x\leq u_x\leq r\leq v_x\leq q_x.
\)
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:ODE-contraction} it suffices to prove that $T$ is a
singular operator of type $(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol p,\boldsymbol q,0)$. Fix rectangles
${\boldsymbol E},{\boldsymbol F}\subseteq\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$. Let us first consider the local Whitney configuration in
Definition~\ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef1}. H\"older's
inequality and the boundedness of $T$ give
\begin{align*}
  \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E}T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E})\bigr\|_{L^r_{t,x}}
  &\lesssim
  |E_t|^{[r,q_t]}|E_x|^{[r,q_x]}
  \bigl\|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E})\bigr\|_{L^{q_t}_tL^{q_x}_x} \\
  &\lesssim
  |E_t|^{[r,q_t]}|E_x|^{[r,q_x]}
  |E_t|^{[p_t,r]}|E_x|^{[p_x,r]}
  \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E}\bigr\|_{L^r_{t,x}} \\
  &=
  |E_t|^{[p_t,q_t]}|E_x|^{[p_x,q_x]}
  \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E}\bigr\|_{L^r_{t,x}}.
\end{align*}
In this configuration we have $|E_t|\lesssim \inf(E_t)$ and
$|E_x|\lesssim \inf(E_t)^{n/m}$, so the final factor is bounded by
$\inf(E_t)^\kappa$, as required. For the configurations in
Definition~\ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef2}-\ref{it:ODEDef3}, the boundedness
assumption immediately yields
\[
    \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol F}T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E})\bigr\|_{L^{q_t}_tL^{q_x}_x}
    \lesssim
    \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E}\bigr\|_{L^{p_t}_tL^{p_x}_x}.
\]
When $\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol p$, $\boldsymbol v=\boldsymbol q$, and
$\kappa=[p_t,q_t]+\frac nm[p_x,q_x]$, the distance powers in
Definition~\ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef2} and
Definition~\ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef3} cancel exactly, while $M=0$. Hence these two
estimates follow.

It remains to check Definition~\ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef4}. Write
$D_t:=\operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)$ and $d_x:=d(E_x,F_x)$. By H\"older's inequality in the
time variable and the boundedness assumption,
\begin{align*}
  \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol F}T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E})\bigr\|_{L^r_tL^{q_x}_x}
  &\lesssim
  |F_t|^{[r,q_t]}
  \bigl\|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E})\bigr\|_{L^{q_t}_tL^{q_x}_x} \\
  &\lesssim
  |F_t|^{[r,q_t]}|E_t|^{[p_t,r]}
  \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E}\bigr\|_{L^r_tL^{p_x}_x} \\
  &\lesssim
  D_t^{[p_t,q_t]}
  \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol E}\bigr\|_{L^r_tL^{p_x}_x}.
\end{align*}
Since
\[
  D_t^{[p_t,q_t]}
  =
  d_x^{-n[p_x,q_x]+m\kappa}
  \Bigl(\frac{D_t}{d_x^m}\Bigr)^{[p_t,q_t]},
\]
this is precisely Definition~\ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef4} with
$\boldsymbol u=\boldsymbol p$, $\boldsymbol v=\boldsymbol q$ and $M=0$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The converse to Proposition \ref{prop:boundedimplySOwithM=0} fails in general. For example, one can find  bounded singular operators on $L^r(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ of type $(0,1, r, (u,u), (v,v), 0)$ which are not bounded from $L^u(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ to $L^v(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$, see Section~\ref{sec:GRT}.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:duality}
    Let  $T$ and $S$ be linear operators $L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)\to L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$  such that for all $f,g\in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$,
    \[
    \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} Tf\cdot \overline g \ \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t =\int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} f\cdot \overline{Sg} \ \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t.
    \]  
    Then $T$ is a singular operator of type $(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v, M)$ if and only if $S$ is a singular operator of type 
    $(\kappa,m,r',\boldsymbol v',\boldsymbol u', M)$, where the parameters are assumed to be in the ranges as in Definition~\ref{def:ODE}.
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:kernelODE}
 Let $r, u_x,v_x\in[1,\infty]$, $\kappa , M\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ and $m\in (0,\infty)$. We say that
  a {linear} operator $T\colon L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+) \to L^0(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ is  a
  \emph{{singular integral operator of type} $(\kappa,m,r,u_x,v_x, M)$} if
  there is a strongly measurable $K \colon \{(t,s) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+^2:t \ne s\} \to \mathcal{L}(L^r(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n))$ such that for all $f \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ we have the kernel representation
  \begin{equation}
      \label{eq:representation} Tf(t,x) = \int_0^\infty \bigl[K(t,s)f(s)\bigr](x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s, \qquad (t,x) \notin \pi(f),
  \end{equation}
   and   there exists a constant $C<\infty$  such that the following assertions hold for all $f \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ and $E_x,F_x \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n$.
  \begin{enumerate}[(i)]
        \item\label{it:Lr} ($L^r$-boundedness) 
        There is a $\gamma\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ such that $T$ is  bounded from $L^r(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+;t^{\gamma r}\mathrm{d} t\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x)$ to {$L^r(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+^{1+n};t^{(\gamma -\kappa) r}\mathrm{d} t\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x)$} 
        with norm $\le C$.
        
        \item \label{item:kernelODE-t-sep} {($t$-separation)} 
        If $t\ne s$, we have
        \[ \bigl\| K(t,s)f(s)\bigr\|_{L^{v_x}_{x}} \leq C \,{\abs{t-s}}^{-1-\frac{n}m[u_x,v_x]+\kappa} \cdot\bigl\|f(s)\bigr\|_{L^{u_x}_{x}}. \]
    
        \item \label{item:kernelODE-x-sep} {($x$-separation)} 
        If {$d(E_x,F_x) \geq c\, |t-s|^{\frac1m}>0$}, we have
        \[ \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{F_x} K(t,s) ( f(s)\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x} )\bigr\|_{L^{v_x}_{x}} \leq C\, d(E_x,F_x)^{-m-n[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa} \left( \frac{\abs{t-s}}{d(E_x,F_x)^m} \right)^{M} \bigl\|f(s) \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x}\bigr\|_{L^{u_x}_{x}}. \]
   \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
Let us make a few comments on Definition \ref{def:kernelODE} and its relation to its precursor in \cite{AH25a, AKMP12}.\label{rem:KernelODE}
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item\label{it:kernelODEAH} Denote by 
    \[ M_{\text{AH}} := M+ 1-\kappa+\tfrac{n}{m}[u_x,v_x]. \]
    When $M_{\text{AH}}\ge 0$, the combination of the $t$- and $x$-separation conditions in Definition \ref{def:kernelODE} is equivalent to 
    \begin{align*}
        \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{F_x} & K(t,s)(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x})\bigr\|_{L^{v_x}_{x}}\le C \abs{t-s}^{-1-\frac{n}{m}[u_x,v_x]+\kappa} \left( 1+\frac{d(E_x,F_x)^m}{\abs{t-s}} \right)^{-M_{\text{AH}}} \bigl\|f \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x}\bigr\|_{L^{u_x}_{x}}.
    \end{align*}  
When $M_{\text{AH}}> 0$, this is exactly the $L^{u_x}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)$-$L^{v_x}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)$ off-diagonal decay of type $(\kappa, m, M_{\text{AH}})$ for the family of operators $K(t,s)$  appearing in \cite[Definition 1]{AH25a}. Hence, our definition of a singular integral operator in Definition \ref{def:kernelODE}  includes the classes SIO$^{\kappa \pm}_{m,q,M_{\text{AH}}}$
of \cite[Definitions 3 and 4]{AH25a} for which {either $q=u_x\le 2$ and $v_x=2$ or $u_x=2$ and $q=v_x\ge 2$} and the integral in the representation \eqref{eq:representation} is limited to either $(0,t)$ or $(t,\infty)$.
\item {When $M_{\text{AH}}>\frac n m $, one can prove the $L^r$-boundedness of $K(t,s)$ for any $r\in [u_x,v_x]$  from the assumed off-diagonal estimates 
{(see, e.g., \cite[Lemma 4.7]{Auscher-Egert2023-book})}. However, when $M_{\text{AH}}\le \frac n m$, this is unclear.}
\item The formulation in Definition \ref{def:kernelODE} involves an operator-valued kernel representation of $T$, hence the addition of ``integral'' in the terminology. In stark contrast, Definition \ref{def:ODE} is free of any representation and also accommodates subadditive operators.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:compareAH}
  Let $r, u_x,v_x\in[1,\infty]$, $\kappa \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$, $m\in (0,\infty)$ and $M> -1$. Let $T$ be a
  {{singular integral operator of type} $(\kappa,m,r,u_x,v_x, M)$}. Then $T$ is a singular operator of type $(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v}, M)$ with $\boldsymbol{u}:=(1,u_x)$ and $\boldsymbol{v}:=(\infty,v_x)$.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Since $\sup(E_t) \eqsim t \eqsim \inf(E_t)$ on Whitney-type regions, it is clear that the weighted $L^r$-boundedness in Definition \ref{def:kernelODE}\ref{it:Lr} implies Definition \ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef1}.
Fix $f \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ and let  ${\boldsymbol{E}},{\boldsymbol{F}} \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$ be rectangles. We will consider  Definition \ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef2}-\ref{it:ODEDef4} separately.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]\setcounter{enumi}{1}
  \item {($t$-separation)} Assuming $d_{t}:=d(E_t,F_t)>0$, we have
\begin{align*}
   \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})\bigr\|_{L^{\infty_{\vphantom{t}}}_tL^{v_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}} &= \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{t \in F_t} \, \Bigl\|x \mapsto \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{F_x}(x) \int_{E_t} \bigl[K(t,s)(f(s)\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x})\bigr](x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s \Bigr\|_{L^{v_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\\
   &\leq \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{t \in F_t} \,\int_{E_t} \Bigl\|x \mapsto \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{F_x}(x)  \bigl[K(t,s)(f(s)\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x})\bigr](x) \Bigr\|_{L^{v_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s\\
   &\lesssim  d_{t}^{-1-\frac{n}m[u_x,v_x]+\kappa} \int_{E_t} \nrm{f(s)\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x}}_{L^{u_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s\\
   &=  d_{t}^{-[1,\infty]-\frac{n}m[u_x,v_x]+\kappa} 
\cdot \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}}\bigr\|_{L^{1_{\vphantom{t}}}_tL^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}},
\end{align*}
as desired.


\item {($t$- and $x$-separation)} Assuming  $d_{t}:=d(E_t,F_t) \geq c^m \cdot D_{t} $ and $d_{x}:=d(E_x,F_x) \geq c\cdot D_{t}^{1/m}$, with $D_{t}:=\operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)$, we have
\begin{align*}
   \bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})\bigr\|_{L^{\infty_{\vphantom{t}}}_tL^{v_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}} &= \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{t \in F_t} \, \Bigl\|x \mapsto \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{F_x}(x) \int_{E_t} \bigl[K(t,s)(f(s)\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x})\bigr](x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s \Bigr\|_{L^{v_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\\
   &\leq \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{t \in F_t} \,\int_{E_t} \Bigl\|x \mapsto \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{F_x}(x)  \bigl[K(t,s)(f(s)\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x})\bigr](x) \Bigr\|_{L^{v_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
   \\&
   \lesssim  d_{x}^{-m-{n}[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa-mM}  
   \cdot \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{t \in F_t} \, \int_{E_t} {\abs{t-s}^M} \nrm{f(s)\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{E_x}}_{L^{u_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
   \\&
   \lesssim  d_{x}^{-m[1,\infty]-{n}[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa} 
   \cdot \Bigl(\frac{D_{t}}{d_{x}^{m}}\Bigr)^M \cdot  \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}}\bigr\|_{L^{1_{\vphantom{t}}}_tL^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}.
\end{align*}
The last inequality is always valid when $M\ge 0$, whereas  $d_{t}\geq c^m\cdot D_{t} $ is used when $M<0$.
\item {($x$-separation)} Assume $d_{x}:=d(E_x,F_x) \geq c \cdot D_{t}^{1/m}$, with $D_{t}:=\operatorname{diam}(E_t\cup F_t)$, but  $E_t$ and $F_t$ are not necessarily separated. Since $M>-1$, we have the estimate
$$
  \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{t\in F_t}\int_{E_t} |t-s|^M \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s\lesssim 
  D_{t}^{M+1},
$$
which yields 
\begin{align*}
\bigl\|\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})\bigr\|_{L^{\infty_{\vphantom{t}}}_tL^{v_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}
& \lesssim d_{x}^{-m[1,\infty]-{n}[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa-mM} 
\cdot D_{t}^{M+[1,\infty]}\cdot  
\bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}}\bigr\|_{L^{\infty_{\vphantom{t}}}_tL^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}.
\end{align*}
The same estimate holds with $L^{\infty}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+)$ replaced by
$L^1(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+)$, using instead that 
$$\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{s \in E_t}\int_{F_t} |t-s|^M \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t\lesssim 
  D_{t}^{M+1}.
$$
The result for $L^r(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+)$ follows from Schur's lemma or interpolation.
\end{enumerate}
This verifies all assumptions of Definition \ref{def:ODE} and completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:pointwiseimmliesnonpointwise} Let us comment on Proposition \ref{prop:compareAH}.
\begin{enumerate}
    
    \item In the proof  we obtained the required estimates for a larger class of rectangles \({\boldsymbol{E}}, {\boldsymbol{F}}\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+\) than those appearing in  Definition \ref{def:ODE}. Furthermore, the \(L^r\)-boundedness of \(K(t,s)\) was not used in the proof.

\item Even when restricting Definition \ref{def:kernelODE} to the same class of rectangles as in Definition \ref{def:ODE}, there is no reason to expect the converse implication in the statement to hold for linear operators.  
\begin{itemize}
    \item   Even if one could recover an operator-valued kernel representation in an appropriate sense, when the parameter \(M\) in the \(x\)-separation condition of Definition \ref{def:ODE} is small, it is not clear how to prove the \(L^r\)-boundedness of \(K(t,s)\) away from the diagonal \(s=t\) as mentioned in Remark~\ref{rem:KernelODE}. Such bounds enter quantitatively in the singular integral theory developed in \cite{AH25a} for $r=2$. 
\item  The local $L^r$-boundedness \ref{it:ODEDef1} in Definition \ref{def:ODE} is strictly weaker than the weighted $L^r$-boundedness assumption \ref{it:Lr} in Definition \ref{def:kernelODE}, and can be implied by other conditions.
\end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:decomposition} Let $T\colon L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+) \to L^0(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ be a subadditive operator.
Then, for any  $f,g \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$, we have
\begin{align*}
\int_{{\mathbb R}^{1+n}_+}\abs{Tf}\abs{g}  \leq
\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}})\bigr|\abs{g} &+ 
\sum_{k=1}^3 \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^k} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^k})\bigr|\abs{g}
\end{align*}
where for $Q \in \mathcal{D}$ we denote its dyadic parent by $\widehat{Q}$ and set $($see Figure \ref{fig:EF-pictures}$\, )$
\begin{align*}
   {\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^1 &:= (0,4^{-m}\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q,  & {\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^1&:= \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}},\\
    {\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^2 &:= (\ell(Q)^m,2^m\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q, & {\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^2&:= (0,2^{-m} \ell(Q)^m)\times Q,\\
    {\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3 &:= (0,2^m\ell(Q)^m)\times ( 3\widehat{Q}\setminus 3{Q} ), & {\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3&:= \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{ca}}.
\end{align*}
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Take ${Q} \in {\mathcal{D}}$. Since $\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{ca}} = \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}\cup\bigcup_{P\in \operatorname{ch}(Q)} \boldsymbol{P}^{\mathrm{ca}}$ modulo null sets, we can decompose
\begin{align*}
  \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{ca}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{ca}}})\bigr||g|&\leq \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{ca}}})\bigr||g| + \sum_{{P} \in \operatorname{ch}\br{{Q}}}\int_{\boldsymbol{P}^{\mathrm{ca}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{ca}}\setminus \widetilde{\boldsymbol{P}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{P}}^{\mathrm{ca}}})\bigr||g| \\&\hspace{1cm}+ \sum_{{P} \in \operatorname{ch}\br{{Q}}} \int_{\boldsymbol{P}^{\mathrm{ca}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{P}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{P}}^{\mathrm{ca}}})\bigr||g|. 
\end{align*}
The terms in the final sum on the right-hand side are of the same form as the left-hand side with $Q$ replaced by its dyadic children, so we can iterate. {Since $g \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$, the distance between the support of $g$ and the boundary $\partial \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$ is strictly positive, so the iteration in the final sum on the right-hand side will be identically zero after a finite number of iterations.}
Starting from a dyadic cube ${Q_0} \in {\mathcal{D}}$  such that $\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{ca}}_0$ contains the supports of $f$ and $g$, we have 
$$ \int_{{\mathbb R}^{1+n}_+}|Tf||g| =  \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{ca}}_0} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{ca}}_0})\bigr||g|$$
and thus the iteration procedure yields, with $\mathcal{D}(Q_0)$ the set of dyadic cubes contained in $Q_0$,  
\begin{align*}
  \int_{{\mathbb R}^{1+n}_+}|Tf||g|&\leq  \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}(Q_0)}\int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{ca}}})\bigr||g| + \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}(Q_0)}\sum_{{P} \in \operatorname{ch}\br{{Q}}}\int_{{\boldsymbol{P}^{\mathrm{ca}}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{ca}}\setminus\widetilde{\boldsymbol{P}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{P}}^{\mathrm{ca}}})\bigr||g|\\
  &\leq \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}(Q_0)} \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}})\bigr||g|+\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}(Q_0)} \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{ca}}\setminus \widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}})\bigr||g| \\&\hspace{1cm}+\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}(Q_0)} \int_{\bigcup_{P\in \operatorname{ch}(Q)} {\boldsymbol{P}^{\mathrm{ca}}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{(\ell(Q)^m,2^m\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q})\bigr||g|
  \\&\hspace{1cm}+\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}(Q_0)} \sum_{{P} \in \operatorname{ch}\br{{Q}}}\int_{{\boldsymbol{P}^{\mathrm{ca}}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{(0,\ell(Q)^m)\times (3Q \setminus 3P)})\bigr||g|.
\end{align*}
Noting that the second, third and fourth terms are bounded precisely by the $k=1,2,3$ terms {(relabelling $P$ as $Q$ in the fourth term)} and dropping the restriction that cubes are subcubes of $Q_0$, this finishes the proof.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
Suppose  $T$ is linear and consider the associated bilinear form \(\int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} Tf\cdot g\). In this case, {all inequalities become equalities} once the absolute values are omitted. Rearranging the terms, one can estimate
\[
\Bigl|\int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} Tf\cdot g-{\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}(Q_0)}} \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}})\cdot g\Bigr|
\]
by the same last three error terms appearing in Proposition \ref{prop:decomposition}.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:esttseparated}
Let $r \in [1,\infty]$, $\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v} \in [1,\infty]^2$, $\kappa, M \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$, and $m\in [1,\infty)$. Let $T$ be a
singular  operator  of type $(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v, M)$. For $Q \in \mathcal{D}$, we recall from Proposition~\ref{prop:decomposition} that
\begin{align*}
    {\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^1 &:= (0,4^{-m}\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q,  & {\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^1&:= \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}},\\
    {\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^2 &:= (\ell(Q)^m,2^m\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q, & {\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^2&:= (0,2^{-m} \ell(Q)^m)\times Q.
\end{align*}
Then we have for any $f,g \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ 
\begin{align*}
\sum_{{Q} \in {\mathcal{D}}} \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^1} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^1})\bigr|\abs{g} &\lesssim \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} t^\kappa\cdot H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{u},\br{2\sqrt{n}}^m}f(t,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol{v}',\br{\sqrt{n}}^m}g(t,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x,\\
\sum_{{Q} \in {\mathcal{D}}} \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^2} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^2})\bigr|\abs{g} &\lesssim \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} t^\kappa\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol{u},\br{2\sqrt{n}}^m}f(t,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{v}',\br{\sqrt{n}}^m}g(t,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x.
\end{align*}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
For the first estimate, fix $Q \in \mathcal{D}$ and note that for $E_t :=  (0,4^{-m}\ell(Q)^m)$ and $F_t:= (2^{-m}\ell(Q)^m, \ell(Q)^m)$ we have $\ell_t = \ell(Q)^m$, $\ell_x = \operatorname{diam}(3Q) = 3\sqrt{n} \ell(Q)$ and
\begin{align*}
    d(E_t,F_t) &= (2^m-1) 4^{-m}\ell(Q)^m\\ 
    \sup(E_t\cup F_t)+ \operatorname{diam}(3Q)^m &\leq \ell(Q)^m+(3\sqrt{n}\cdot \ell(Q))^m \leq (4\sqrt{n}\cdot \ell(Q))^m
\end{align*}
Therefore, we obtain by H\"older's inequality and the $t$-separated case of Definition \ref{def:ODE} that
\begin{align} \begin{aligned}  \label{eq:toffest}
 \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} &\bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{(0,4^{-m}\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q})\bigr|\abs{g}\\
 &\lesssim  \ell(Q)^{-m[u_t,v_t]-{n}[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa}
 \cdot\bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{(0,4^{-m}\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q}\bigr\|_{L^{\vphantom{{v'_{\vphantom{t}x}}}u_t}_tL^{\vphantom{{v'_{\vphantom{t}x}}}u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}  \cdot \bigl\|g\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}\bigr\|_{L^{{v'_t}}_tL^{{v'_{\vphantom{t}x}}}_{\vphantom{t}x}} \\
  &\lesssim \ell(Q)^{m+n+m\kappa} \inf_{(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{u},\br{2\sqrt{n}}^m}f(2^mt,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol{v}',\br{\sqrt{n}}^m}g(2^mt,x),
\end{aligned}
\end{align}
where in the last step we used that for any $(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}$ we have $2^mt \geq \ell(Q)^m$ and thus
\begin{align*}
    (0,4^{-m}\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q &\subseteq (0,2^m t)\times B(x,{(\br{2\sqrt{n}}^m\cdot2^mt)^{1/m}}),\\
    \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}&\subseteq (2^{-m}t,2^m t)\times B(x,{(\br{\sqrt{n}}^m\cdot2^mt)^{1/m}}).
\end{align*}
Hence, using  the disjointness of the  Whitney regions, $\abs{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}\eqsim \ell(Q)^{m+n}$ and $t \eqsim \ell(Q)^m$ for all $(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}$, we deduce
\begin{align*}
  \sum_{{Q} \in {\mathcal{D}}} \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} &\bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{(0,4^{-m}\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q})\bigr|\abs{g}\\ &\lesssim \sum_{{Q} \in {\mathcal{D}}}\int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} t^\kappa\cdot H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{u},\br{2\sqrt{n}}^m}f(2^mt,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol{v}',\br{\sqrt{n}}^m}g(2^mt,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\\
  &\lesssim \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} t^\kappa\cdot H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{u},\br{2\sqrt{n}}^m}f(t,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol{v}',\br{\sqrt{n}}^m}g(t,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x,
\end{align*}
using a change of variables in the last step. 
The second estimate is proven analogously.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
We state Lemma~\ref{lem:esttseparated} and all results that follow only for \(m\geq 1\) to avoid technicalities. Indeed, as \(m\downarrow 0\), the factor \(2^m-1\) tends to \(0\), so the fixed geometric constant \(c>0\) would have to be chosen depending on \(m\). For each fixed \(m>0\), one could choose \(c>0\) sufficiently small instead. Since our applications only involve \(m=1,2\), we choose not to complicate the notation.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
Let $T\colon L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+) \to L^0(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ be an operator.
\begin{itemize}
    \item We call  $T$ \emph{causal} if for all $f \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ and ${\boldsymbol{E}}=E_t\times E_x$  with  $E_t \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+$  and $E_x\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n$ we have
\begin{align*}
    T(f \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})(t,x) &= 0, & & \makebox[0pt][l]{\ensuremath{(t,x)\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+:\ t<\inf E_t.}}\hphantom{(t,x) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}
\end{align*}
\item We call  $T$ \emph{anti-causal} if for all $f \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ and ${\boldsymbol{E}}=E_t\times E_x$  with  $E_t \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+$  and $E_x\subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n$ we have
\begin{align*}
    T(f \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{E}})(t,x) &= 0, & & \makebox[0pt][l]{\ensuremath{(t,x)\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+:\ t>\sup E_t.}}\hphantom{(t,x) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}
\end{align*}
\end{itemize}
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:maindominationform}
Let $r\in[1,\infty]$, $\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v} \in [1,\infty]^2$, $\kappa,M \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ and $m\in [1,\infty)$. Let $T$ be a
singular  operator  of type $(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v, M)$.
Then we have for any $f,g \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ that
\begin{align*}
\int_{{\mathbb R}^{1+n}_+}&\abs{Tf}\abs{g} 
\lesssim 
\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \ell(Q)^{m\kappa} \cdot \ip{f}_{r,\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}\cdot \ip{g}_{\vphantom{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}r',\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \cdot\abs{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}
&& \\
&+\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-jm\br{M+[u_t,v_t]-\kappa}} \cdot \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}t^\kappa\cdot   H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r,u_x),2^{jm}}f(t,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r',v_x'), 2^{jm}}g(t,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t  &&
\text{$(\mathrm{w}$-$\mathrm{w})$}\\
&+\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-jm\br{M+[u_t,v_t]-\kappa}} \cdot \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}t^\kappa\cdot   H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{u},2^{jm}}f(t,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol{v}', 2^{jm}}g(t,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t &&\text{$(\mathrm{ca}$-$\mathrm{w})$}\\
&+\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-jm\br{M+[u_t,v_t]-\kappa}} \cdot
\int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}t^\kappa\cdot   H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol{u},2^{jm}}f(t,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{v}', 2^{jm}}g(t,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t. &&\text{$(\mathrm{w}$-$\mathrm{ca})$}.
\end{align*}
If $T$ is causal, the term {$(\mathrm{w}$-$\mathrm{ca})$} is omitted, and if $T$ is anti-causal, the term {$(\mathrm{ca}$-$\mathrm{w})$} is  omitted.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Using Proposition \ref{prop:decomposition}, we decompose
\begin{align}\label{eq:decompinproof}
\int_{{\mathbb R}^{1+n}_+}\abs{Tf}\abs{g}  \leq
\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}})\bigr|\abs{g} &+ 
\sum_{k=1,2,3} \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^k} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^k})\bigr|\abs{g}
\end{align}
where $E_Q^k$ and $F_Q^k$ for $k=1,2,3$ are as in Proposition \ref{prop:decomposition}. For the first term on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:decompinproof} we have by Definition \ref{def:ODE}\ref{it:ODEDef1}
\begin{align*}
\sum_{{Q} \in {\mathcal{D}}} \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}})\bigr|\abs{g} &\leq \sum_{{Q} \in {\mathcal{D}}}
\nrm {T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}})}_{\vphantom{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}L^{r}(\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}})} \cdot \nrm {g}_{\vphantom{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}L^{r'}(\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}})} \\
&\lesssim \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \ell(Q)^{m\kappa} \cdot \ip{f}_{r,\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}} \cdot \ip{g}_{\vphantom{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}} r',\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}\cdot \abs{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}},
\end{align*}
which matches the first term on the right-hand side of our claim. The $t$-separated terms in \eqref{eq:decompinproof},
i.e., those involving  ${\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^k$ and ${\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^k$ for $k=1,2$, are handled by Lemma \ref{lem:esttseparated},
and are dominated by terms {$(\mathrm{w}$-$\mathrm{ca})$} and {$(\mathrm{ca}$-$\mathrm{w})$}.
It remains to analyse 
$$
    \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3})\bigr|\abs{g},
$$
using the $x$-separated case and the $t$- and $x$-separated case in Definition~\ref{def:ODE}.

\medskip

Fix $Q \in \mathcal{D}$ and recall that
\begin{align*}
    {\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3 &:= (0,2^m\ell(Q)^m)\times (3\widehat{Q}\setminus 3{Q}), & {\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3&:= \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{ca}}.
\end{align*}
Note that these sets are $x$-separated. Indeed, one has $\ell_t^{1/m} = 2\ell(Q) \le 6\sqrt{n} \ell(Q) = \ell_x$, and
\[ c\ell_x \le \ell(Q) = d(3\widehat{Q}\setminus 3{Q},Q). \]
To exploit the decay when the $x$-separation is much bigger than the $t$-separation, we further decompose the $t$-interval dyadically.
For $j \geq 0$, define the following {intervals and strips}
\begin{align*}
  R_j&:= (2^{-jm} \ell(Q)^m,2^{-(j-1)m}\ell(Q)^m),&& \boldsymbol{R}_j:= R_j\times \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n,\\
   \widetilde{R}_j&:= (2^{-(j+1)m} \ell(Q)^m,2^{\min\{-(j-2),1\}m}\ell(Q)^m),&& \widetilde{\boldsymbol{R}}_j:= \widetilde{R}_j\times \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n,\\
 {R}^{\mathrm{ca}}_j&:= (0,2^{-(j+1)m}\ell(Q)^m), && \boldsymbol{R}^{\mathrm{ca}}_j:={R}_j^{\mathrm{ca}}\times \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n,
\end{align*}
and set $\boldsymbol{Q}_j:= R_j\times Q$.
Note that, up to  null sets, ${R}^{\mathrm{ca}}_j = \bigcup_{k\ge j+2} {R}_k$ and $\widetilde{R}_j = \bigcup_{|k- j|\le 1, k\ge 0} {R}_k$, and therefore
\begin{align*}
    (0,2^m\ell(Q)^m)\times (0,2^m\ell(Q)^m)= \bigcup_{j=0}^\infty \bigcup_{k=0}^\infty R_j\times R_k = \bigcup_{j=0}^\infty R_j \times \widetilde{R}_j \cup \bigcup_{j=0}^\infty R_j \times {R}_j^{\mathrm{ca}} \cup \bigcup_{j=0}^\infty  {R}_j^{\mathrm{ca}} \times R_j.
\end{align*} 
Hence, we can decompose further as follows
\begin{align*}
     \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3})\bigr|\abs{g} &\leq \sum_{j=0}^\infty \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \widetilde{\boldsymbol{R}}_j})\bigr|\abs{g} + \sum_{j=0}^\infty\int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j^{\mathrm{ca}}})\bigr|\abs{g}\\&\hspace{2cm}+\sum_{j=0}^\infty\int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j^{\mathrm{ca}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j})\bigr|\abs{g}\\&=: \text{\framebox[15pt]{A}}+\text{\framebox[15pt]{B}}+\text{\framebox[15pt]{C}},
\end{align*}
{where the sets in \text{\framebox[15pt]{B}} and \text{\framebox[15pt]{C}} are separated in both $t$ and $x$. Indeed, observe that $$c^m \ell_t = c^m 2^m 2^{-jm} \ell(Q)^m \le (1-2^{-m})2^{-jm}\ell(Q)^m = d(R_j,R_j^{\mathrm{ca}}).$$}

Let us first consider \framebox[15pt]{A}. Note that $\boldsymbol{E}_Q^3$ is a finite union of rectangles in $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+^{1+n}$, so the estimates in Definition \ref{def:ODE} are applicable. Fix $j\geq 0$. By 
 H\"older's inequality and the $x$-separated case in Definition~\ref{def:ODE},  we can estimate 
\begin{align}\label{eq:Aestimatebegin}\begin{aligned}
    \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \widetilde{\boldsymbol{R}}_j})\bigr|\abs{g} &\lesssim  \ell(Q)^{-n[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa}\cdot 2^{-jm(M+[u_t,v_t])}   \\&\hspace{1cm} 
    \cdot \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \widetilde{\boldsymbol{R}}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{\vphantom{r'_{\vphantom{x}}}r}_{t}L^{\vphantom{r'_{\vphantom{x}}}u_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\cdot \bigl\|g\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{r'_{\vphantom{x}}}_{t}L^{v_x'}_{\vphantom{t}x}}.
\end{aligned} 
\end{align} 
Now note that for $(t,x)  \in \boldsymbol{Q}_j$ we have
\begin{align*}
 \widetilde{R}_j\times (3\widehat{Q}\setminus 3{Q} )&\subseteq (4^{-m} t,4^m t)\times B(x,{(2^{jm}\cdot \br{\sqrt{n}}^m\cdot 4^mt)^{1/m}}),
\end{align*}
and thus 
\begin{align}\label{eq:whitestf}\begin{aligned}
 \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \widetilde{\boldsymbol{R}}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{r_{\vphantom{x}}}_{t}L^{u_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}}
   &\leq \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{(4^{-m} t,4^m t)\times B(x,{(2^{jm}\cdot\br{\sqrt{n}}^m\cdot4^mt)^{1/m}})}\bigr\|_{L^{r_{\vphantom{x}}}_{t}L^{u_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}} \\
   &\lesssim (2^{-j}\ell(Q))^{\frac{m}{r}} \ell(Q)^{\frac n{u_x}}\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r,u_x), 2^{jm}\br{\sqrt{n}}^m }f(4^mt,x).\end{aligned}
\end{align} 
Similarly, we have for $(t,x)  \in \boldsymbol{Q}_j$
\begin{align}\label{eq:whitestg}
  \bigl\|g\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{r'_{\vphantom{x}}}_{t}L^{v'_x}_{\vphantom{t}x}} \lesssim  
  (2^{-j}\ell(Q))^{\frac{m}{r'}} \ell(Q)^{\frac n{v_x'}}
  \cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r',v_x'), 2^{jm}\br{\sqrt{n}}^m }g(4^mt,x).
\end{align} 
Combining \eqref{eq:Aestimatebegin}, \eqref{eq:whitestf}, and \eqref{eq:whitestg}, we conclude 
\begin{align*}\begin{aligned}
  \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \widetilde{\boldsymbol{R}}_j})\bigr|\abs{g}&\lesssim  2^{-jm[u_t,v_t]-jmM}\cdot  2^{-jm}\ell(Q)^{m+n+m\kappa} \\&\cdot \inf_{(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}_j} H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r,u_x),2^{jm}\br{\sqrt{n}}^m}f(4^mt,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r',v_x'), 2^{jm} \br{\sqrt{n}}^m }g(4^mt,x).
\end{aligned}\end{align*}
Now note that $2^{-jm} \ell(Q)^{m+n} \eqsim \abs{\boldsymbol{Q}_j}$
{and that $t\eqsim (2^{-j}\ell(Q))^m$ for $(t,x)\in \boldsymbol{Q}_j$}. Furthermore, note that for almost all fixed $(t,x)\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$ and all $j \geq 0$ there is a unique $Q \in \mathcal{D}$ such that $(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}_j$. Therefore, we obtain {
\begin{align*}\begin{aligned}
      {\sum_{{Q} \in \mathcal{D}}}\text{\framebox[15pt]{A}}&\lesssim \sum_{{Q} \in \mathcal{D}} \sum_{j=0}^{\infty}  2^{-jm(M+[u_t,v_t]-\kappa)}\\&\hspace{2cm}\cdot \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}_j} t^\kappa\cdot   H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r,u_x),2^{jm}\br{\sqrt{n}}^m}f(4^mt,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r',v_x'), 2^{jm} \br{\sqrt{n}}^m }g(4^mt,x) \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\\
  &\lesssim \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-jm(M+[u_t,v_t]-\kappa)} \cdot \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}t^\kappa\cdot   H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r,u_x),2^{jm}}f(t,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r',v_x'), 2^{jm} }g(t,x) \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x
\end{aligned}
\end{align*} }
after a change of variables and a shift in the $j$ indices, giving an estimate by term {$(\mathrm{w}$-$\mathrm{w})$}.

Consider next the term \framebox[15pt]{B}.
Applying
the off-diagonal estimate from the $t$- and $x$-separated case in Definition~\ref{def:ODE}
gives that
\begin{align}\begin{aligned} \label{eq:Btermstart}
    \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap\boldsymbol{R}_j} 
    \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}^{\mathrm{ca}}_j})\bigr|\abs{g} &\lesssim  \ell(Q)^{-m[u_t,v_t]-n[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa}\cdot 2^{-jmM} \\
    &\hspace{1cm} \cdot 
    \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap {\boldsymbol{R}}^{\mathrm{ca}}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{\vphantom{v'_{t}}u_{t}}_{t}L^{\vphantom{v'_{t}}u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\cdot 
    \bigl\|g\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{v'_{t}}_{t}L^{v'_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}},
\end{aligned} 
\end{align} 
where
$$
 \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap {\boldsymbol{R}}_j^{\mathrm{ca}}}\bigr\|_{L^{u_{t}}_{t}L^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}} 
  \lesssim (2^{-j}\ell(Q))^{\frac{m}{u_t}} \ell(Q)^{\frac n{u_x}}\cdot H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol u, 2^{jm}\br{2\sqrt{n}}^m }f(2^mt,x)
$$
and 
$$
  \bigl\|g\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{v'_{t}}_{t}L^{v'_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}} \lesssim  
  (2^{-j}\ell(Q))^{\frac{m}{v_t'}} \ell(Q)^{\frac n{v_x'}}
  \cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol v', 2^{jm}\br{\sqrt{n}}^m }g(2^mt,x).
$$
Collecting these estimates as for \framebox[15pt]{A}
gives an estimate by term {$(\mathrm{ca}$-$\mathrm{w})$}.
Finally, the estimate     
$$
{\sum_{{Q} \in \mathcal{D}}}\text{\framebox[15pt]{C}}\lesssim    \sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-jm(M+[u_t,v_t]-\kappa)}\cdot  \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}t^\kappa\cdot   H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol{u},2^{jm}}f(t,x)\cdot H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{v}', 2^{jm} }g(t,x) \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x
$$
is similar, which gives the stated domination.


If $T$ is causal, we note that \framebox[15pt]{C} and the term involving ${\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^2$ and ${\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^2$ in \eqref{eq:decompinproof} are zero. Hence, we do not get a Carleson type operator on $g$ in any of the estimates. Similarly, if $T$ is anti-causal, then \framebox[15pt]{B} and the term involving ${\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^1$ and ${\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^1$ in \eqref{eq:decompinproof} are  zero.  Hence, in this case we do not get a Carleson type operator on $f$ in any of the estimates.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:quasimaindominationform}
Let \(\nu\in(0,1)\), $r\in[1,\infty]$, $\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{v} \in [1,\infty]^2$,  $\kappa, M \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ and $m \in [1,\infty)$. 
Let $T$ be a
singular  operator  of type $(\kappa,m,r,\boldsymbol u,\boldsymbol v, M)$.
Then, for any $f,g \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ 
\begin{align*}
&\int_{{\mathbb R}^{1+n}_+}\abs{Tf}^\nu\abs{g} 
\lesssim 
\sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \ell(Q)^{ \nu m\kappa} \cdot \ip{f}_{r,\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}^\nu \cdot \ip{g}_{\vphantom{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}({r}/{\nu})',\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}^{}\cdot \abs{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}
&& \\
&+\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-jm\nu\br{M+[u_t,v_t]-\kappa}} \cdot \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}t^{\nu\kappa}\cdot   (H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r,u_x),2^{jm}}f(t,x))^\nu\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\vphantom{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}(( r/\nu)',({v_x}/\nu)'), 2^{jm}}g(t,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t  &&\text{$(\mathrm{w}$-$\mathrm{w})$}\\
&+\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-jm\nu\br{M+[u_t,v_t]-\kappa}} \cdot \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}t^{\nu\kappa}\cdot   (H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{u},2^{jm}}f(t,x))^\nu\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{({\boldsymbol{v}}/\nu)', 2^{jm}}g(t,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t &&\text{$(\mathrm{ca}$-$\mathrm{w})$}\\
&+\sum_{j=0}^{\infty} 2^{-jm\nu\br{M+[u_t,v_t]-\kappa}} \cdot
\int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+}t^{\nu\kappa}\cdot   (H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol{u},2^{jm}}f(t,x))^\nu\cdot H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{({\boldsymbol{v}}/\nu)', 2^{jm}}g(t,x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t. &&\text{$(\mathrm{w}$-$\mathrm{ca})$}
\end{align*}
If $T$ is causal, the term {$(\mathrm{w}$-$\mathrm{ca})$} is omitted, and if $T$ is anti-causal, the term {$(\mathrm{ca}$-$\mathrm{w})$} is  omitted.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
The proof follows that of Theorem~\ref{thm:maindominationform}, using the 
  decomposition~\eqref{eq:pdecomp} instead. Therefore, we only point out the differences.
The argument for the first term on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:pdecomp} becomes
\begin{align*}
\sum_{{Q} \in {\mathcal{D}}} \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}})\bigr|^\nu\abs{g} &\leq \sum_{{Q} \in {\mathcal{D}}}
\nrm {T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}})}_{\vphantom{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}L^{r}(\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}})}^\nu \cdot\nrm {g}^{\vphantom{\nu}}_{\vphantom{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}L^{( r/\nu)'}(\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}})} \\
&\lesssim \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \ell(Q)^{ \nu m\kappa} \cdot \ip{f}_{r,\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}^\nu \cdot \ip{g}^{\vphantom{\nu}}_{\vphantom{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}({r}/{\nu})',\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}\cdot \abs{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}},
\end{align*}
which again matches the first term on the right-hand side of our claim.  
The H\"older estimate replacing \eqref{eq:toffest} for the term $k=1$ is
\begin{align*} 
 \int_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} &\bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{(0,4^{-m}\ell(Q){^m})\times 3Q})\bigr|^\nu\abs{g}\\
 &\lesssim  \Big(\ell(Q)^{-m[u_t,v_t]-{n}[u_x,v_x]+{m}\kappa} \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{(0,4^{-m}\ell(Q)^m)\times 3Q}\bigr\|_{L^{u_{t}}_{t}L^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\Big)^\nu
 \cdot\bigl\|g\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}\bigr\|_{L^{(v_t/\nu)'}_{t}L^{(v_x/\nu)'}_{\vphantom{t}x}} \\
  &\lesssim \ell(Q)^{m+n+m\kappa \nu} \inf_{(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} (H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol{u},\br{2\sqrt{n}}^m}f(2^mt,x))^\nu\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(\boldsymbol{v}/\nu)',\br{\sqrt{n}}^m}g(2^mt,x),
\end{align*}
using that 
\begin{equation}  \label{eq:pduality}
 -\nu[u_t,v_t]+\nu/u_t+ 1/(v_t/\nu)'=1= 
-\nu[u_x,v_x]+\nu/u_x+ 1/(v_x/\nu)'.   
\end{equation}
The estimate replacing \eqref{eq:Aestimatebegin} for term \framebox[15pt]{A}, using \eqref{eq:pduality}, is
\begin{align*}
    \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j} &\bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \widetilde{\boldsymbol{R}}_j})\bigr|^\nu\abs{g} \\
    &\lesssim  \Big(\ell(Q)^{-n[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa}\cdot 2^{-jm(M+[u_t,v_t])}
     \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap \widetilde{\boldsymbol{R}}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{r_{\vphantom{t}}}_{t}L^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\Big)^\nu
     \cdot \bigl\|g\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{(r_{\vphantom{t}}/\nu)'}_{t}L^{(v_x/\nu)'}_{\vphantom{t}x}} \\
     &\lesssim  2^{-jm\nu([u_t,v_t]+M)}\cdot  2^{-jm}\ell(Q)^{m+n+m\kappa \nu} \\
     &\hspace{1cm}\cdot \inf_{(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}_j} (H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(r,u_x),2^{jm}\br{\sqrt{n}}^m}f(4^mt,x))^\nu\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{((r/\nu)',(v_x/\nu)'), 2^{jm} \br{\sqrt{n}}^m }g(4^mt,x), 
\end{align*}
which leads to an estimate by term {$(\mathrm{w}$-$\mathrm{w})$}.
The estimate replacing \eqref{eq:Btermstart} for term \framebox[15pt]{B}, using \eqref{eq:pduality}, is
\begin{align*}
    \int_{{\boldsymbol{F}}_Q^3\cap\boldsymbol{R}_j} &
    \bigl|T(f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap  \boldsymbol{R}^{\mathrm{ca}}_j})\bigr|^\nu\abs{g} \\
    &\lesssim  \Big(\ell(Q)^{-m[u_t,v_t]-n[u_x,v_x]+m\kappa}\cdot 2^{-jmM} 
    \bigl\|f\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{{\boldsymbol{E}}_Q^3\cap {\boldsymbol{R}}^{\mathrm{ca}}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{u_{t}}_{t}L^{u_{\vphantom{t}x}}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\Big)^\nu
    \cdot\bigl\|g\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{F}_Q^3\cap \boldsymbol{R}_j}\bigr\|_{L^{(v_t/\nu)'}_{t}L^{(v_x/\nu)'}_{\vphantom{t}x}}\\
     &\lesssim  2^{-jm\nu([u_t,v_t]+M)}\cdot  2^{-jm}\ell(Q)^{m+n+m\kappa \nu} \\
     &\hspace{1cm}\cdot \inf_{(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}_j} (H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol u,2^{jm}\br{2\sqrt{n}}^m}f(2^mt,x))^\nu\cdot H^{\mathrm{w}}_{(\boldsymbol v/\nu)', 2^{jm} \br{\sqrt{n}}^m }g(2^mt,x), 
\end{align*} 
which leads to an estimate by term {$(\mathrm{ca}$-$\mathrm{w})$}. The term \framebox[15pt]{C} is handled similarly, and the causal and anti-causal discussion is identical to that in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:maindominationform}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- prop-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:equivnorms}
  Let $p,q,r \in (0,\infty]$, fix $0<a<b<\infty$ and $c>0$.
    Replacing $W_r f$ by 
    \begin{align*}
  W^{a,b,c}_{r}f(t,x)
  :=  \Bigl(    \fint_{at}^{bt}
    \fint_{B(x, (ct)^{1/m})}
    |f(s,y)|^r \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} y \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
  \Bigr)^{1/r},
  \qquad (t,x)\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+,
\end{align*}
in the definition of the tent space norms
yields (quasi-)norms equivalent to $\nrm{f}_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}$.
<!-- end prop-7 -->
<!-- prop-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:dyadic}
Let $p,q,r \in (0,\infty]$ and $\beta \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$. For $Q \in \mathcal{D}$, define
\[
  W_{r,Q}(f) := \Bigl( \fint_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}} \abs{f(t,y)}^r \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} y \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \Bigr)^{1/r}.
\]
If $p<\infty$, then
\[
  \nrm{f}_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta} \eqsim \bigl\|\cbrace{W_{r,Q}(f)}_{Q \in \mathcal{D}}\bigr\|_{t^{p,q}_\beta}:=\Bigl\| \Bigl( \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \ell(Q)^{m-m\beta q}\cdot  W_{r,Q}(f)^q \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_Q \Bigr)^{1/q} \Bigr\|_{L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)}.
\]
If $p=\infty$, then
$$
 \nrm{f}_{T^{\infty,q,r}_\beta} \eqsim \bigl\|\cbrace{W_{r,Q}(f)}_{Q \in \mathcal{D}}\bigr\|_{t^{\infty,q}_\beta}:=
 \sup_{Q_0\in\mathcal{D}}
 \Bigl( \fint_{Q_0}\sum_{Q\in \mathcal{D}(Q_0)}
 \ell(Q)^{m-m\beta q}\cdot  W_{r,Q}(f)^q \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_Q(x) \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x
 \Bigr)^{1/q},
$$
with the usual modifications  when $q=\infty$.
<!-- end prop-8 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
The proof is a straightforward generalization of \cite[Propositions 3.12 and 3.13]{Haa26} to $m\ge 1$. In the proofs there, it suffices to use 
  Proposition~\ref{prop:equivnorms} instead of a precise change of angle for the norms.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- prop-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:tentspacedensityduality} 
Let $p,q,r\in (0,\infty]$ and $\beta\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
    \item\label{it:density} $L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ is dense in $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$ if $\max\{p,q,r\}<\infty$ and weak-star dense if  $\min\{p,q,r\}>1$.
    \item\label{it:duality} If $\min\{p,q,r\} \ge  1$, the K\"othe dual of $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$ is
$T^{p',q',r'}_{-\beta}$.
In particular 
$$
  \nrm{f}_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}\eqsim
  \sup_g\int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} |f(t,x)|\cdot |g(t,x)| \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x,
$$
where the supremum is taken over all $g\in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ with 
$\nrm{g}_{T^{p',q',r'}_{-\beta}}=1$.
\item\label{it:quasiduality} If $0<\nu \le \min(p,q,r)$, 
\begin{equation*} 
  \|f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_{\beta}}^\nu \eqsim \sup_{g} \int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} |f(t,x)|^\nu \cdot|g(t,x)| \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x,
\end{equation*}  
where the supremum is taken over all $g\in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ with $\|g\|_{T^{(p/\nu)',(q/\nu)', (r/\nu)'}_{-\beta \nu}} = 1$.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-9 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
{Strong density in \ref{it:density}  follows from a standard approximation argument and weak-star density follows as a consequence of \ref{it:duality}.}
For \ref{it:duality} we note that, after a change of variables $s=t^m$ to reduce to the case $m=1$ and in our notation, \cite[Theorem 5.2]{Hua16} states  that 
\begin{align}\label{eq:multiplierkothe}
    T^{p',q',r'}_{-\beta} = \mathcal{M}(T^{p,q,r}_\beta, T^{1,1,1}_0) = \mathcal{M}(T^{p,q,r}_\beta, L^1(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)).
\end{align}
Here, $\mathcal{M}(T^{p,q,r}_\beta, L^1(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+))$ denotes the space of all multipliers from $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$ to $L^1(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$, i.e., all $g \in L^0(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_{+}^{1+n})$ such that $f \mapsto gf$ is a bounded operator from $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$ to $L^1(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$. Hence, \eqref{eq:multiplierkothe}  is exactly the same as saying that $T^{p',q',r'}_{-\beta}$ is the K\"othe dual of $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$. 
Now by the Lorentz-Luxemburg theorem (see \cite[Theorem~71.1]{Za67}), we know that
$$
  \nrm{f}_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}\eqsim
  \sup_{g}\int_{\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+} |f(t,x)|\cdot |g(t,x)| \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x,
$$
where the supremum is taken over all $g \in T^{p',q',r'}_{-\beta}$ with $\nrm{g}_{T^{p',q',r'}_{-\beta}} = 1$. Finally, we note that it suffices to take the supremum over $g \in L^\infty_c(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+)$ by truncations and monotone convergence. 
Finally, \ref{it:quasiduality} follows from the power rule formula \eqref{eq:rescalenorm} and \ref{it:duality} applied with $p/\nu, q/\nu, r/\nu$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rem:p<1}
Even though the dual of $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$ in the quasi-Banach range $\min\{p,q,r\}<1$ has been identified in \cite[Theorems 3.23 and 3.25]{Haa26}, this  is not of use in our analysis. Indeed, since the 
Lorentz-Luxemburg theorem does not hold for quasi-Banach function spaces, we cannot use the dual of $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$ to calculate the norm of $f \in T^{p,q,r}_\beta$ in this range. Instead, we will use Proposition \ref{prop:tentspacedensityduality}\ref{it:quasiduality}, which is based on the power rule \eqref{eq:rescalenorm}. However, the dual of $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$ can be used to deduce boundedness results for the adjoints {$T^*$ of linear singular operators $T$ to which our statements apply}.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lemma:Whitneymap}
Let $p,q,r \in (0,\infty]$, $\beta,\kappa \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$ . Then
$$
  A_{r,\kappa}^{\mathrm{w}} f:=  \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \ell(Q)^{m\kappa} \cdot \ip{f}_{r,\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}} \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}, \qquad f\in L^0(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+),
$$
defines a bounded operator  from $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$ to $T^{p,q,r}_{\beta+\kappa}$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Consider first $p<\infty$. Applying first Proposition~\ref{prop:dyadic} and then 
Proposition~\ref{prop:equivnorms}, we estimate
\begin{align*}
    \nrm{A_{r,\kappa}^{\mathrm{w}}f }_{T^{p,q,r}_{\beta+\kappa}} &\eqsim \Bigl\| \Bigl( \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \ell(Q)^{m-m(\beta+\kappa) q}\cdot  W_{r,Q}\bigl(\ell(Q)^{m\kappa}\cdot  \ip{f}_{r,\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}} \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}}\bigr)^q \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_Q \Bigr)^{1/q} \Bigr\|_{L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)}\\
    &= 
    \Bigl\| \Bigl( \sum_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \ell(Q)^{m-m\beta q}\cdot  \Bigl(\fint_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}|f|^r\Bigr)^{q/r} \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_Q \Bigr)^{1/q} \Bigr\|_{L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)} \\
    &\lesssim
    \bigl\|(t,x)\mapsto t^{-\beta} W^{a,b,c}_r f(t,x)
    \bigr\|_{L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n; L^q(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+))} \\
    &\eqsim\nrm{f}_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}, 
\end{align*}
using that for suitable $a,b,c$ we have
$\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}\subseteq (at,bt)\times B(x,(ct)^{1/m})$
for $x\in Q$ and $2^{-m}\ell(Q)^m\le t\le \ell(Q)^m$.

For $p=\infty$, we similarly estimate 
\begin{align*}
   \nrm{A_{r,\kappa}^{\mathrm{w}}f}_{T^{\infty,q,r}_{\beta+\kappa}} 
    &\eqsim
 \sup_{Q_0\in\mathcal{D}}
 \Bigl( \fint_{Q_0}\sum_{Q\in \mathcal{D}(Q_0)}
 \ell(Q)^{m-m\beta q}\cdot  \Bigl(\fint_{\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}}|f|^r\Bigr)^{q/r}  \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_Q(x) \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x
 \Bigr)^{1/q}\\
    &\lesssim
    \sup_{\tau>0}\sup_{y\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n} \Bigl( 
  \int_0^\tau \fint_{B(y,\tau^{1/m})} |t^{-\beta}W^{a,b,c}_r f(t,x)|^q \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \Bigr)^{1/q} \\
    &\eqsim\nrm{f}_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}, 
\end{align*}
again by embedding 
$\widetilde{\boldsymbol{Q}}\vphantom{\boldsymbol{Q}}^{\mathrm{w}}\subseteq (at,bt)\times B(x,(ct)^{1/m})$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:slice}
    Let $p,u \in (0,\infty)$, $q,r \in (0,\infty]$ with $u\leq r$, $\beta \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}$  and $\delta \ge 1$ and $\varepsilon>0$. Set
\[
  \gamma
  :=\tfrac{n}{m}
  \bigl[\min\cbrace{p,q,u},u\bigr].
\]
Then we have for all $f \in T^{p,q,r}_\beta$
\[
  \nrm{A_{u,\delta}f}_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}
  \lesssim
  \delta^{\gamma+\varepsilon}\,
  \|f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta},
\]
The implicit constant is independent of $\delta$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
By Proposition \ref{prop:dyadic}, it suffices to bound the discrete sequence norm $\nrm{ \{ W_{r,Q}(A_{u,\delta} f) \}_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} }_{t^{p,q}_\beta}$. 
For $\delta\ge 1$, there exists an integer $J$, only depending on $n,m$ and $\delta$, such that the index set 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:J}
 \Lambda_\delta := \bigl\{ k \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}^n : \abs{k}_\infty \le 2^J \bigr\},
\end{equation}
  (where $\abs{k}_\infty$ denotes the max-norm) has  cardinality \(N:=\abs{\Lambda_\delta}\eqsim \delta^{n/m}\) and we have the uniform covering
\[
  B(x, (\delta t)^{1/m}) \subseteq \bigcup_{k \in \Lambda_\delta} (Q + k \ell(Q))
\]
for all $Q \in \mathcal{D}$ and $(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}$. Indeed, this is obtained by translating and rescaling a corresponding covering for the unit dyadic cube.

 Fix a dyadic cube $Q \in \mathcal{D}$. For $k \in \Lambda_\delta$ let $Q_k := Q + k\ell(Q)$ denote the shifted dyadic cubes. For all $(t,x) \in \boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}$ we have by the covering and Jensen's inequality
\begin{align*}
  A_{u,\delta} f(t,x) 
  &= \Bigl( \fint_{B(x, (\delta t)^{1/m})} \abs{f(t,z)}^u \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} z \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{u}} \\
  &\lesssim \Bigl( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k \in \Lambda_\delta} \fint_{Q_k} \abs{f(t,z)}^u \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} z \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{u}} \\
  &\le \Bigl( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k \in \Lambda_\delta} \Bigl( \fint_{Q_k} \abs{f(t,z)}^r \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} z \Bigr)^{\frac{u}{r}} \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{u}}.
\end{align*}
Fix $\nu < \min\{p, q, u\}$ such that $\gamma_\nu := \frac{n}{m} [\nu,u] =\gamma+\varepsilon$.
Since the right-hand side is independent of $x$, averaging this over $\boldsymbol{Q}^{\mathrm{w}}$ and using Minkowski's inequality since $u\le r$, we obtain 
\begin{align}\label{eq:whitofav}
\begin{aligned}
  W_{r,Q}(A_{u,\delta} f) &\lesssim
  \Bigl(\fint_{2^{-m}\ell(Q)^m}^{\ell(Q)^m}\Bigl( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k \in \Lambda_\delta} \Bigl( \fint_{Q_k} \abs{f(t,z)}^r \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} z \Bigr)^{\frac{u}{r}} \Bigr)^{\frac{r}{u}} \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t\Bigr)^{1/r}
  \\ &\leq\Bigl( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k \in \Lambda_\delta} W_{r,Q_k}(f)^u \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{u}} \\
  &\leq N^{\frac{1}{\nu} - \frac{1}{u}} \Bigl( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k \in \Lambda_\delta} W_{r,Q_k}(f)^\nu \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{\nu}} \\
  &\eqsim \delta^{\gamma_\nu} \Bigl( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k \in \Lambda_\delta} W_{r,Q_k}(f)^\nu \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{\nu}}. 
\end{aligned}
\end{align}
This estimate also holds for $r=\infty$ with the usual modifications. 

Define for $j\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$, 
\[
  F_j(y) := \sum_{P \in \mathcal{D}: \ell(P) = 2^{-j}} W_{r,P}(f)^\nu \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_P(y), \qquad y \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n.
\]
Note that when $\ell(Q)=2^{-j}$, 
\[ \fint_{\cup_{k \in \Lambda_\delta } Q_k} F_j(y)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} y= \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k \in \Lambda_\delta} W_{r,Q_k}(f)^\nu.
\] 
As $\cup_{k \in \Lambda_\delta } Q_k$ is a region contained within a ball centered at $x$ of radius $\eqsim \delta^{\frac{1}{m}}\ell(Q)$ and of measure $\eqsim \delta^{\frac{n}{m}}\abs{Q}$, we obtain 
\[ 
  \Bigl( \frac{1}{N} \sum_{k \in \Lambda_\delta} W_{r,Q_k}(f)^\nu \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{\nu}} \lesssim \bigl( {M}(F_j)(x) \bigr)^{\frac{1}{\nu}},
\]
where ${M}$ denotes the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator.


Let us now evaluate the $t^{p,q}_\beta$-sequence norm. By partitioning the sum over all $Q \in \mathcal{D}$ into scales $j \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$, and using the fact that the cubes at a fixed scale $j$ partition $\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
  \bigl\| \{ W_{r,Q}(A_{u,\delta} f) \}_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \bigr\|_{t^{p,q}_\beta}
  &= \Bigl\| \Bigl( \sum_{j \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}} \sum_{\ell(Q)=2^{-j}} 2^{-jm+jm\beta q} \cdot W_{r,Q}(A_{u,\delta} f)^q \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_Q \Bigr)^{1/q} \Bigr\|_{L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)} \\
  &\lesssim \delta^{\gamma_\nu} \Bigl\| \Bigl( \sum_{j \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}} 2^{-jm+jm\beta q}\cdot {M}(F_j)^{q/\nu} \Bigr)^{1/q} \Bigr\|_{L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)}\\
  &= \delta^{\gamma_\nu} \Bigl\| \Bigl( \sum_{j \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}} 2^{-jm+jm\beta q}\cdot {M}(F_j)^{q/\nu} \Bigr)^{\nu/q} \Bigr\|_{L^{p/\nu}_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)}^{1/\nu}.
\end{align*}
Now, using that  $q/\nu>1$ and $p/\nu>1$, the vector-valued Fefferman--Stein 
maximal inequality \cite{FS71}, which trivially also holds when $q=\infty$, yields 
\begin{align*}
  \bigl\| \{ W_{r,Q}(A_{u,\delta} f) \}_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \bigr\|_{t^{p,q}_\beta}
  &\lesssim \delta^{\gamma_\nu } \Bigl\| \Bigl( \sum_{j \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}} \bigl( 2^{-jm\nu/q+jm\beta \nu}\cdot {M}(F_j) \bigr)^{q/\nu} \Bigr)^{\nu/q} \Bigr\|_{L^{p/\nu}_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)}^{1/\nu} \\
  &\lesssim \delta^{\gamma_\nu } \Bigl\| \Bigl( \sum_{j \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}} \bigl( 2^{-jm\nu/q+jm\beta \nu} \cdot F_j \bigr)^{q/\nu} \Bigr)^{\nu/q} \Bigr\|_{L^{p/\nu}_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)}^{1/\nu} \\
  &= \delta^{\gamma_\nu} \Bigl\| \Bigl( \sum_{j \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}} \sum_{\ell(Q)=2^{-j}}  2^{-jm+jm\beta q}\cdot W_{r,Q}(f)^q \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_Q \Bigr)^{1/q} \Bigr\|_{L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n)} \\
  &= \delta^{\gamma +\varepsilon} \bigl\| \{ W_{r,Q}(f) \}_{Q \in \mathcal{D}} \bigr\|_{t^{p,q}_\beta}.
\end{align*}
Applying Proposition \ref{prop:dyadic} yields the claimed estimate.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{remark:noepsilonloss}
   The $\varepsilon$-loss in Lemma~\ref{lem:slice} can be avoided in two cases. First, if $\min\{p,q\}>u$, one may take $\nu=u$ in the proof, which directly gives the estimate with $\varepsilon=0$. Indeed, the only place where we used $\nu<\min\{p, q, u\}$ is in the application of the vector-valued Fefferman--Stein inequality, which only used $\nu <\min\cbrace{p,q}$.  
   
   Second, if $q\leq p,u$, one may also take $\varepsilon=0$. Indeed, taking $\nu=q$ in \eqref{eq:whitofav}, raising to the $q$-th power, and dualizing the resulting $L^{p/q}$-norm, one can reindex the shifted dyadic cubes and reduce the estimate to the scalar Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator. 
   
   We do not need these refinements below and leave the details to the interested reader.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- prop-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:modelops-whitneymixed}
Let \(p \in (0,\infty)\), $q,r \in (0,\infty]$, \(\beta\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\), \(\delta\in[1,\infty)\) and $\varepsilon>0$. Let
\(\boldsymbol u\in(0,\infty)^2\) satisfy \(u_t,u_x\le r\) and set
\begin{align*}
  \gamma
  :=
  \tfrac{n}{m}
  {\bigl[\min\cbrace{p,q,u_x},u_x\bigr].}
\end{align*}
For all $f \in T^{p,q,r}_{\beta}$ we have
  \begin{align*}
    \nrm{H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f}_{T^{p,q,r}_{\beta}}
    \lesssim  \delta^{\gamma+\varepsilon}\,\nrm{f}_{T^{p,q,r}_{\beta}}.
  \end{align*}
 If $
    \beta>\gamma-[u_t,q]$, 
    we also have
  \begin{align*}
    \nrm{H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f}_{T^{p,q,r}_{\beta}}
    \lesssim
    \delta^{\gamma+\varepsilon}\,
    \nrm{f}_{T^{p,q,r}_{\beta}}.
  \end{align*}
 The implicit constants are independent of $\delta$.
<!-- end prop-10 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
The claim for $H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}$ follows almost immediately from Lemma \ref{lem:slice}. Indeed, since $u_t\le r$, Jensen's inequality in the $s$-average gives for $(t,x) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$
\begin{align*}
      H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f(t,x) &=
\Bigl(\fint_{c^m t}^t\Bigl(\fint_{B(x,(\delta t)^{1/m})} \abs{f(s,y)}^{u_x} \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} y\Bigr)^{\frac{u_t}{u_x}} \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s\Bigr)^{\frac{1}{u_t}}\\  
  &\lesssim
  \Bigl(
    \fint_{c^m t}^t
    A_{u_x,c^{-m}\delta}f(s,x)^r\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
  \Bigr)^{1/r}.
\end{align*}
Therefore, for $(\tau,z) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$
\begin{align}\label{eq:AudomHw}
\begin{aligned}
      W_r(H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f)(\tau,z)
  &\lesssim
  \Bigl(\fint_{2^{-m} \tau}^\tau
    \fint_{B(z,\tau^{1/m})}
    \fint_{c^m t}^t
    A_{u_x,c^{-m}\delta}f(s,x)^r\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t
  \Bigr)^{1/r} \\
  &\lesssim
  \Bigl(
    \fint_{(c/2)^{m} \tau}^\tau
    \fint_{B(z,\tau^{1/m})}
    A_{u_x,c^{-m}\delta}f(s,x)^r\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
  \Bigr)^{1/r}.
\end{aligned}
\end{align}
On the right-hand side, we are integrating over a $t$-enlarged Whitney region. Therefore, taking $L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n;L^q_\beta(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+))$-norms and applying  
 Lemma \ref{lem:slice}, we conclude 
\[
  \|H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}
  \lesssim
  \|A_{u_x,c^{-m}\delta}f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}
  \lesssim
  \delta^{\gamma+\varepsilon} \|f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}.
\]


To prove the claim for $H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}$, fix $(t,x) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$. Define $I_k(t):= (c^{m(k+1)}t ,c^{mk}t )$ for $k\geq 0$ and decompose
\[
  (0,t )=\bigcup_{k=0}^\infty I_k(t)
\]
modulo null sets.
Define $\nu:=\min\cbrace{p,q,u_t}$. Then, since for $s \in I_k(t)$ we have $t \leq  c^{-m(k+1)}s \leq c^{-m} t$, we can estimate
\begin{align}\label{eq:pointdomHw}
\begin{aligned}
  H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f(t,x)
  &=
  \Bigl(
    \sum_{k=0}^\infty
    \frac{|I_k(t)|}{t }    \fint_{I_k(t)}
    \Bigl(      \fint_{B(x,(\delta t )^{1/m})}|f(s,y)|^{u_x}\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} y
    \Bigr)^{u_t/u_x}    \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
  \Bigr)^{1/u_t} \\
  &\lesssim
  \Bigl(\sum_{k=0}^\infty
  c^{\nu mk/u_t}  \Bigl(
    \fint_{I_k(t)}
    \Bigl(
      \fint_{B(x,(\delta t )^{1/m})}|f(s,y)|^{u_x}\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} y
    \Bigr)^{u_t/u_x}
    \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
  \Bigr)^{\nu/u_t}\Bigr)^{1/\nu}.\\
 &\lesssim
  \Bigl(\sum_{k=0}^\infty
  c^{\nu mk/u_t}  \Bigl(
    \fint_{I_k(t)}
    A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+1)}\delta}f(s,x)^{u_t}
    \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
  \Bigr)^{\nu/u_t}\Bigr)^{1/\nu}.
\end{aligned}
\end{align}
Taking the $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$-norm and using \eqref{eq:convex}
we obtain
\begin{equation}\label{eq:estHcafirst}
  \|H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta} \lesssim \Bigl( \sum_{k=0}^\infty c^{\nu mk/u_t} \cdot \Bigl\|(t,x)\mapsto \Bigl(
    \fint_{I_k(t)}
    A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+1)}\delta}f(s,x)^{u_t}
    \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
  \Bigr)^{1/u_t} \Bigr\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}^\nu \Bigr)^{1/\nu}.
\end{equation}
We will analyse the norm on the right-hand side for fixed $k\geq 0$. For $(\tau,z) \in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^{1+n}_+$ the Whitney average of the $T^{p,q,r}_\beta$-norm can, by Jensen's inequality, be estimated as follows
\begin{align*}
  \Bigl( \fint_{2^{-m}\tau}^\tau &\fint_{B(z,\tau^{1/m})} \Bigl( \fint_{I_k(t)} A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+1)}\delta}f(s,x)^{u_t} \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s \Bigr)^{\frac{r}{u_t}} \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} t \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{r}}\\&\lesssim \Bigl( \fint_{c^{m(k+1)}2^{-m}\tau}^{c^{mk}\tau} \sup_{x \in B(z, \tau^{1/m})} A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+1)}\delta}f(s,x)^r  \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{r}}\\
  &\leq \Bigl( \fint_{c^{m(k+1)}2^{-m}\tau}^{c^{mk}\tau} \sup_{x \in B(z, {2c^{-(k+1)}s^{1/m}})} A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+1)}\delta}f(s,x)^r  \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{r}}\\
  &\lesssim \Bigl( \fint_{c^{m(k+1)}2^{-m}\tau}^{c^{mk}\tau} A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+2)}\delta}f(s,z)^r \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s \Bigr)^{\frac{1}{r}},
\end{align*}
where we used \eqref{eq:martingale} in the final step.
Taking the $L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n; L^q_\beta(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+))$-norm and first performing a change of variables $\sigma = c^{mk}\tau$ and then reintroducing the spatial average using \eqref{eq:martingaleback}, we obtain
\begin{align}\label{eq:dilatedest}
\begin{aligned}
    \Bigl\|&(t,x)\mapsto \Bigl(
    \fint_{I_k(t)}
    A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+1)}\delta}f(s,x)^{u_t}
    \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s
  \Bigr)^{1/u_t} \Bigr\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta} \\&\lesssim  c^{mk(\beta - \frac{1}{q})} \Bigl\|(\sigma,z)\mapsto \Bigl( \fint_{c^m2^{-m}\sigma}^\sigma A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+2)}\delta}f(s,z)^r \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s \Bigr)^{1/r} \Bigr\|_{L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n; L^q_\beta(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+))}\\
  &\lesssim c^{mk(\beta - \frac{1}{q})} \Bigl\|(\sigma,z)\mapsto \Bigl( \fint_{c^m 2^{-m}\sigma}^\sigma \fint_{B(z, \sigma^{1/m})} A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+3)}\delta}f(s,w)^r \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} w \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} s \Bigr)^{1/r} \Bigr\|_{L^p_{\vphantom{\beta}}(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n; L^q_\beta(\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}_+))} \\
  &\lesssim c^{mk(\beta - \frac{1}{q})} \|A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+3)}\delta}f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta},
\end{aligned}
\end{align}
where in the last step we used Proposition~\ref{prop:equivnorms}.
Combining with \eqref{eq:estHcafirst} and Lemma \ref{lem:slice}, we conclude
\begin{align*}
  \|H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}
  &\lesssim  \Bigl(\sum_{k=0}^\infty  c^{\nu mk(\beta+[u_t,q])}  \|A_{u_x, c^{-m(k+3)}\delta}f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}^\nu\Bigr)^{1/\nu}\\
  &\lesssim
  \delta^{\gamma+\varepsilon}
  \Bigl(\sum_{k=0}^\infty
  c^{\nu mk(\beta+[u_t,q]-\gamma-\varepsilon)}\Bigr)^{1/\nu}
  \|f\|_{T^{p,q,r}_\beta}.
\end{align*}
Since $0<c<1$, the series converges whenever
\[
  \beta+[u_t,q]-\gamma>\varepsilon.
\]
Since we may shrink $\varepsilon>0$ if necessary, this finishes the proof when $r<\infty$. If $r=\infty$, the usual modifications apply.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- prop-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:cabddp>infty}
Let $q,r\in (0,\infty]$, \(\beta\in\ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}\), \(\delta\in[1,\infty)\). Let
\(\boldsymbol u\in(0,\infty)^2\) satisfy \(u_t,u_x\le r\) and set
\begin{align*}
  \gamma
  :=
  \tfrac{n}{m} {\bigl[\min\cbrace{q,u_x},u_x\bigr]}.
\end{align*}
For all $f \in T^{\infty,q,r}_{\beta}$ we have
  \begin{align*}
    \nrm{H^{\mathrm{w}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f}_{T^{\infty,q,r}_{\beta}}
    \lesssim  \delta^{\gamma}(1+\ln \delta)^{\frac1q}\,\nrm{f}_{T^{\infty,q,r}_{\beta}},
  \end{align*}
 and if $
    \beta>\gamma-[u_t,q]$, we also have
  \begin{align*}
    \nrm{H^{\mathrm{ca}}_{\boldsymbol u,\delta}f}_{T^{\infty,q,r}_{\beta}}
    \lesssim
    \delta^{\gamma} (1+\ln \delta)^{\frac1q}\,
    \nrm{f}_{T^{\infty,q,r}_{\beta}},
  \end{align*}
  where the implicit constants are independent of $\delta$.
<!-- end prop-11 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
We only consider the case $q<\infty$, the case $q= \infty$ follows by the usual modifications. We first estimate the averaging operator $A_{u,\delta}$ from 
\eqref{eq:avop} for $u\le r$, using the dyadic characterization of $T^{\infty,q,r}_\beta$ from 
Proposition~\ref{prop:dyadic}.
Let $J$ be the integer in \eqref{eq:J}
and recall that
$2^{nJ} \eqsim N  =  \abs{\Lambda_\delta} \eqsim \delta^{n/m}$. Fix $Q^0\in\mathcal{D}$ and
consider the $j$-th generation of children of $Q^0$, denoted by $\mathcal{D}_j(Q^0)$.
It follows as in
\eqref{eq:whitofav}, replacing the embedding $\ell^q \hookrightarrow \ell^u$ by Jensen's inequality in case $q \geq u$, that
\begin{align*}
    \fint_{Q^0}&\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{D}_j(Q^0)} 
    W_{r,Q}(A_{u,\delta}f)^q \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_Q(x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x
    =2^{-jn}\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{D}_j(Q^0)} 
     W_{r,Q}(A_{u,\delta}f)^q\\
    &\lesssim 2^{-jn}\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{D}_j(Q^0)} 
    \Bigl(\frac 1N\sum_{k\in \Lambda_\delta} W_{r,Q_k}(f)^{u} \Bigr)^{q/u} \\
     &\lesssim  2^{-jn}\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{D}_j(Q^0)} \delta^{\gamma_u q}
    \cdot {\frac 1N\sum_{k\in \Lambda_\delta} W_{r,Q_k}(f)^q } \\
    &=2^{-jn}\cdot \frac{\delta^{\gamma_u q}}{N}\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{D}_j(Q^0)} 
    \sum_{k\in \Lambda_\delta} \frac{1}{|Q_k|} \int_{Q_k} W_{r,Q_k}(f)^q  \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{Q_k}(x) \hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x 
    \\
    &= \frac{\delta^{\gamma_u q}}{N} \cdot \frac1{|Q^0|}\int_{R_j} G_j(x) \sum_{Q\in\mathcal{D}_j(Q^0)} 
     \sum_{k\in \Lambda_\delta}\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{Q_k}(x)\hspace{2pt}\mathrm{d} x,
\end{align*}
where
$\gamma_u:=\tfrac{n}{m}\brac{\min\cbrace{q,u},u}$,  $R_j:= \bigcup_{Q\in \mathcal{D}_j(Q^0),\, k\in \Lambda_\delta} Q_k$  and 
$$
 G_j(x)\colon = \sum_{Q\in\mathcal{D}: \ell(Q)= 2^{-j}\ell(Q^0)} 
    W_{r,Q}(f)^q \operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_Q(x), \qquad x\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n.
$$
Note that, by the disjointness of the dyadic cubes at scale $j$, we have for all $x\in \ensuremath{\mathbb{R}}^n$,
\[
\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{D}_j(Q^0)} 
     \sum_{k\in \Lambda_\delta}\operatorname{\mathbf{1}}_{Q_k}(x) \le \min \bigl\{\abs{\mathcal{D}_j(Q^0)}, |\Lambda_\delta|\bigr\}\lesssim \min ( 2^{nj}, 2^{nJ}) \eqsim {N\cdot 2^{-n\max(J-j, 0)}}.
\]
Moreover, by the definition of $\Lambda_\delta$  we have 
\begin{itemize}
    \item If $0\le j<J$, then $R_j$ is contained in the union of $3^n$ dyadic cubes of side length $2^{J-j} \ell(Q^0)$ and
has measure $\eqsim 2^{n(J-j)} \abs{Q^0}$.
\item If $j \geq J$, then $R_j$ is contained in $3Q^0$, which is the union of $3^n$ dyadic cubes of side length $\ell(Q^0)$, and $R_j$ contains $Q^0$, hence has measure $\eqsim |Q^0|$.
